summary: General Heriberto Jara International Airport (VER) serves the historic port city of Veracruz on Mexico's Gulf Coast, named after the Mexican Revolutionary general and former Veracruz governor. As the primary air gateway to one of Mexico's oldest and most culturally rich cities, it handles both domestic flights and limited international connections. The airport sits roughly 10 kilometers southeast of the city center, convenient for travelers heading to the coastal malecón and colonial downtown.
faqs:
Q: How far is the airport from Veracruz city center?
A: The airport is approximately 10 kilometers (about 15 minutes by car) from the historic downtown and malecón area.

Q: Does the airport offer international flights?
A: Yes, it has limited international service to U.S. destinations including Houston and Dallas/Fort Worth, alongside robust domestic connectivity.

Q: Are there currency exchange services available?
A: Yes, currency exchange bureaus and ATMs are available in the terminal building, though better rates are typically found in the city.

Q: What facilities are available for waiting passengers?
A: The terminal offers restaurants, cafés, duty-free shopping, car rental counters, and free Wi-Fi throughout the main areas.
transport_tips: Authorized taxis and pre-booked ride services are available outside the terminal and offer fixed rates to the malecón and downtown Veracruz. Rental cars from major agencies can be arranged in advance for greater flexibility exploring the Gulf Coast region. Shared shuttle services and public buses also connect the airport to central Veracruz at a lower cost than taxis.
local_tip: If you have a layover or early morning arrival, visit Café La Parroquia in Veracruz's historic center—it's a local institution famous for its独特 coffee preparation technique where servers pour hot coffee from a great height to create a distinctive foam.
